questions: Did slalom line_loss_events fall from 0.35 toward 0, and did slalom max_error stay at or above 0.06 m?
Did slalom progress rise above 0.34, and did the first off-track event move later along the course?
Did steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom rise above about 0.5 with the wider span, indicating the 23 mm spacing is adding jitter at edge crossings?
Did the oval and s-bend finish rates hold near iteration 3 (0.85 and 0.30), confirming the wider sensors do not cost other tracks?

intent: Restore the iteration-3 track (0.10 m), which beat the 0.08 m track on score, oval, s-bend and slalom progress. Widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.07 m with 7 sensors at about 23 mm spacing and 16 mm footprints, to test whether sensor reach is what is losing the tape on the slalom. Mass 0.6 kg, body 0.12 x 0.10 m, lead 0.05 m and wheel radius 0.03 m are unchanged, so the sensor-reach change is read alone against iteration 3.
learning: Iteration 4 showed that narrowing wheel_track to 0.08 m hurt every track (score 493.2 to 355.9, s-bend finish 0.30 to 0.05, slalom progress 0.34 to 0.19), so turn authority is not the slalom limit. Iteration 3's slalom still lost the line 0.35 times per run with max_error at the 0.06 m floor, which points to outer sensor reach at ±0.06 m. This iteration tests that reach directly on the 0.10 m track. If line loss stays at 0.3 or more, the next lever is the controller's kd or base_speed (reported to the Integrator), not further geometry.
rationale: Iteration 4 narrowed wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.08 m, and the score fell from 493.2 to 355.9. Oval finish rate dropped from 0.85 to 0.55, s-bend finish from 0.30 to 0.05 with progress 0.75 to 0.66, and slalom progress from 0.34 to 0.19. Steering oscillation on the s-bend rose to 0.45, so the sharper turn was overshooting and the narrow track did not help any development track. The track change is therefore rejected and wheel_track returns to 0.10 m, the iteration-3 value. Iteration 3 is still the best design. Its remaining failure is the slalom, which finished 0 of 20 with line_loss_events 0.35 and max_error 0.0624, just over the 0.06 m off-track floor. Body width cannot move that floor (max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 m for any body under 0.19 m). The Integrator's feedback rule for this case (line loss at 0.3 or more with max_error at or above 0.06 m means the outer sensors are losing the tape at the edge) applies to the iteration-3 slalom data. So I widen the outer sensors from x = ±0.06 to ±0.07 m, keeping 7 sensors and 16 mm footprints, with spacing about 23 mm. Mass 0.6 kg and body 0.12 x 0.10 m stay as in iteration 3, and lead stays at 0.05 m. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0, slalom progress rises above 0.34, and oval and s-bend finish rates hold near iteration 3. The risk is that the wider span adds steering oscillation, so I ask for the oscillation figures to be reported.
